operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces; still double-quote in generated SQL.
Tiny tables: country=3 rows, price/data=398, production=692; no huge-table sampling needed.

production.ID is a single column with THREE FKs (price.ID, data.ID) plus it is a composite-PK member; fks dict keyed by (child_t,child_c) can only hold ONE parent per column -> last-wins collision, must survive.
production.ID FK to data.ID and price.ID: both parents are 1:1 with each other in original (same 398 ids) but TS fills them independently, so child values may match one parent and not the other.
Composite PK (ID, model_year) on production; ID alone is not unique there (398 distinct over 692 rows).
All columns notnull=0, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes; only PKs constrain. So insert failures are rare (PK dupes only).
Declared types INTEGER/REAL/TEXT only; all dispatch to Number/String, no crash-fallback, no Date/Time/Bool/Bit.
Storage classes match declared types everywhere (integer/real/text); no contradictions.
REAL columns hold values like 25561.59078 (price) and 18.0 (mpg); Number fuzzer scale for REAL = default (no args) -> wide range.
model_year values 1970..1982 (13 distinct) but declared INTEGER -> Number fuzzer, NOT Year (type has no 'year').
country.origin 1..3 and country.country text USA/Europe/Japan; production.country FK to origin.
No views/triggers/indexes in DDL; empty-clone is just 4 CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer everywhere: INTEGER -> ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale default (no parens) = 0? -> actually scale from args absent -> upstream default; expect huge/negative ints for mpg-like INTEGER cols (cylinders, horsepower, weight, model, model_year).
REAL columns (price, mpg, displacement, acceleration) get floats over full range plus +-0.01/0.02 perturbation; implausible values (negative mpg, price 1e6) -> likely FN on range predicates.
String fuzzer for car_name and country.country: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings + contamination; car_name predicates (LIKE '%ford%') will mostly miss -> FN.
country.country has only 3 values; String fuzzer with p=0.2 fresh draws will still emit random strings, breaking joins/equalities on country text -> FN.

FK fill: production.ID drawn from price.ID (or data.ID, whichever wins the dict) with replacement; production.country from country.origin (3 values) -> many duplicate (ID,model_year) pairs dropped by PK filter, shrinking production.

Composite PK (ID,model_year): sample_fresh_primary_keys keeps first occurrence; with ID from 398 parents and model_year random ints, collisions rare but model_year random ints make year predicates (model_year=1970) mostly false -> FN.
price.ID and data.ID both 1..398 in original; TS draws them independently so data.ID and price.ID diverge -> joins data-price on ID still work (both random ints) but ties to production.ID break.
No NOT NULL/CHECK so almost all rows insert; only PK dupes skipped -> row counts near target.

Missing ties/duplicates: original has 1:1 ID across price/data/production; TS random ints give few accidental matches -> joins return few rows, may cause FP where gold expects empty vs non-empty or vice versa.
Aggregates (AVG(mpg), COUNT) over random values give different numbers but same shape; order-by/top-k queries sensitive to random ties -> FP/FN.
No Date/Time columns so no date-template misses; no crash-fallback columns.
